matches.rationale: GT1 concerns overgeneralization in the abstract claiming consistent improvements with <1% parameters. Finding 4 identifies contradictory claims in Section 5.1 about inconsistent improvements, which is related but addresses a different location and manifestation of the issue.

GT2 concerns inconsistency in the diagonal scaling matrix definition (claiming ω_i ≠ ω_j but later stating equivalence when equal). None of the findings address this specific logical inconsistency in the method section.

GT3 concerns manipulated accuracy values in Table 1 that exaggerate HyperET's gains. Finding 4 notes contradictory claims about Table 1 results but describes the opposite problem (understatement of benefits), not data manipulation.

GT4 concerns unfair comparison in Section 5.2 due to unreported training budget differences. Finding 5 directly identifies this issue, noting HyperET used extended schedule and augmented compute budget not matched in baselines.

GT5 concerns misrepresentation of prior work in Section 2.3 related work, overstating novelty. Finding 1 identifies a citation placeholder error in Section 2.3 but does not address the substantive issue of fabricated claims about prior art.
GT6 concerns manipulated values in Table 3 ablation study exaggerating flexibility gains. None of the findings address Table 3 or the scaling matrix flexibility ablation.

GT7 concerns overstated rhetoric in the Conclusion about 'large margins' and 'effectively bridging gaps.' Finding 3 identifies an orphaned figure in the Conclusion but does not address rhetorical overstatement.
GT8 concerns omission of ethical considerations and limitations discussion. None of the findings address missing ethical or fairness discussions.

GT9 concerns incoherence between Sections 4.2 and 4.3 about whether diagonal matrices equal scalar scaling or represent distinct parameterization. None of the findings address this cross-section inconsistency.

GT10 concerns incomplete reporting of experimental details (learning rates, batch sizes, iterations) affecting reproducibility. None of the findings specifically identify missing hyperparameter or training protocol details.
GT11 concerns inflated accuracy values in Table 4 for vision encoder ablations. None of the findings address Table 4 or vision encoder comparisons.

GT12 concerns flawed algebraic manipulations in appendix theorem derivations for hyperbolic radius scaling. Finding 2 directly identifies mathematical errors in Appendix Theorem 1, noting incorrect claims about approximation when exact equality holds.

GT13 concerns removal/muting of Möbius multiplication ablation results that demonstrate its necessity. Finding 6 identifies contradictory text claiming similar results regardless of multiplication operation, which obscures the ablation's findings.
